correctness.rationale: The elementary derivation D_w lowers the active-variable count and is therefore locally nilpotent; abelianization restricts exactly to B_i -> B_i^ab, so its kernel, fibers and graded dimensions follow directly. The global rank threshold combines this construction with the published rank-two zero-detection theorem.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The recent source proves only the rank-two zero-detection statement, while older located literature focuses on rank-two locally nilpotent derivations or rank-three automorphisms. Targeted searches found no higher-rank affine-fiber theorem or the same graded kernel formula.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp structural boundary at rank three and quantifies how abelianization loses locally nilpotent derivations: every elementary commutative action acquires an infinite-dimensional affine family of lifts, with an explicit Hilbert series.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
